ProtT5 Zinc Finger Prediction — Interpretation Report

Source: ProtT5_zinc_finger_clean_pipeline.ipynb  |  Model: ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 • 1024-dim  |  Task: Binary classification (Zinc-finger vs Non-zinc-finger)

1. Dataset

UniProtKB Swiss-Prot reviewed proteins split by the Zinc finger annotation column:

  • Positive (Zinc-finger): proteins with at least one annotated ZN_FING feature
  • Negative (non-zinc-finger): proteins with no zinc finger annotation
  • Mutual exclusivity enforced — no protein appears in both sets
  • Duplicate protein names removed (keep first)
Class Imbalance Warning: The dataset is imbalanced (~1:9 ratio). All classifiers use imbalance correction (LR: class_weight="balanced"; MLP: BCEWithLogitsLoss(pos_weight)). PR-AUC is a more informative metric than ROC-AUC under imbalance.

2. Methods

2.1 Full-protein Pooled Embeddings

ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 (Elnaggar et al., 2022) produces 1024-dimensional per-residue representations, aggregated to fixed-length protein vectors via:

  • Max pooling — element-wise maximum over residues
  • Attention pooling — learned weighted average over residues

All features z-score normalised (StandardScaler fit on train only). 80/20 stratified split, seed 42.

2.2 Zinc-finger Domain 21-mer Window Embeddings

Per-residue ProtT5 embeddings (.pt files, shape L×1024) are loaded for each protein. A 21-residue window is centred on the midpoint of the first annotated UniProt ZN_FING domain range and mean-pooled to a 1024-dim vector. Additionally, 3 random non-domain windows from the same protein (positive label) are included, and equal-count random windows from non-zinc-finger proteins (negative label) are added.

ParameterValue
Window size21 residues (10 on each side of domain midpoint)
PoolingMean over window residues → 1024-dim vector
Non-domain windows per protein3
Negative windowsRandom windows from non-zinc-finger proteins
ClassifierMLP: 1024→256→64→1 (binary), 30 epochs, Adam lr=1e-3

2.3 Classifiers (full-protein)

ModelArchitectureImbalance handling
Logistic RegressionL2 penalty, lbfgs, max_iter=5000class_weight="balanced"
MLP (PyTorch) Linear(1024→512)→ReLU→Dropout(0.3)→ Linear(512→128)→ReLU→Dropout(0.3)→Linear(128→1), Adam lr=1e-3, 30 epochs, batch=64, BCEWithLogitsLoss pos_weight = n_neg / n_pos

4. Zinc-finger Domain 21-mer Window Analysis

This analysis tests whether a 21-residue window centred on the annotated zinc-finger domain (as defined by UniProt ZN_FING feature) carries sufficient discriminative signal to distinguish zinc-finger from non-zinc-finger regions using only local sequence context. Windows are mean-pooled from per-residue ProtT5 embeddings (L×1024).

Interpretation: Comparing the domain window ROC-AUC (0.9684) to the full-protein best (0.9921) suggests the full-protein context provides additional discriminative power beyond the local zinc-finger domain. A high domain window score indicates ProtT5 encodes distinct local chemistry around zinc-finger domains.

5. Recommendations for Future Work

  1. Cross-validation: Use 5-fold stratified CV to reduce variance from single splits.
  2. Hard negatives: Use structurally similar non-zinc-finger proteins as hard negatives.
  3. All domains: Use all annotated ZN_FING ranges per protein, not just the first.
  4. Window sweep: Compare window sizes 11, 21, 41, 61 for optimal context.
  5. Ankh / ESM2 comparison: See sibling notebooks for cross-model comparison.
  6. Fine-tuning: End-to-end fine-tune ProtT5 for zinc-finger prediction.
